Automation can be used to check for errors in scientific manuscripts, and inform authors about possible corrections. In this study we examine the usefulness of metacheck to improve best practices.

Participants will imagine a depressed person as more likely to be overweight, less likely to take care of themselves, less likely to be successful at work, with a less attractive face, and more introverted compared to an actor that is explicitly described as not depressed and to a control condition.

Children (aged 8 to 13) who will be exposed to awe-inspiring art will show greater prosocial helping behavior than children who will be exposed to art that evokes other positive emotions (i.e., joy) or an emotionally neutral stimulus.

Experiment - A researcher randomly assigns treatments to study subjects, this includes field or lab experiments. This is also known as an intervention experiment and includes randomized controlled trials.
No blinding is involved in this study.
Two conditions. In one, researchers receive automated feedback. In the control condition, they do not receive feedback.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of six conditions, between-subjects, as two factors will be manipualated (target gender: male vs. female, and status: depressed vs. not depressed vs. control). first participants will be assigned to either the male or the female condition:
Male condition:
Jonathan Smith is a bank clerk at LMS, a bank in New Orleans, Louisiana. He is originally from Houston, Texas. Jonathan is 38, has a Associate Degree in Management, and is Caucasian.
Female condition:
Jessica Smith is a bank clerk at LMS, a bank in New Orleans, Louisiana. She is originally from Houston, Texas. Jessica is 38, has a Associate Degree in Management, and is Caucasian.
Then, participants will be assigned to the depression condition, the nondepression condition, or the control condition. Participants in the control condition will proceed to the questions without reading any additional text.
Participants in the depression condition will read this:
This person is clinically depressed. They often have insomnia and are in a state of a really bad mood.
Participants in the nondepression condition will read this:
This person is not depressed. They have their up and downs like everyone, but are overall quite OK psychologically speaking.

Three conditions in a between-subjects design: awe condition (awe-evoking film clip), joy condition (joy-evoking film clip), control condition (film clip that evokes neither awe nor joy). The videos used in each condition will be selected based on the results of a pilot study that pre-tested whether different film clips evoke the intended emotions.
We randomly assign to conditions
Registration prior to creation of data
We will include all scientists who are willing to participate.
We randomly assigned 50 scientists to a condition where their manuscript was automatically checked for errors, and 50 scientists to a control condition with a checklist.

800 Mturkers.

According to a power analysis, to detect a small to medium effect size with .80 statistical power and alpha error probability of .05, we need:
(1) 158 participants in the above specified negative binomial regression test
(2) 124 participants in the above specified Fisher's exact test
Therefore, we aim to collect data from 158 children aged 8 to 13 to satisfy the power needs of the more demanding statistical test.

Based on an a-priori power analysis for an independent t-test, with an expected effect size of d = 0.6, an alpha of 0.05, and a desired power of 0.85, we needed to collect at least 50 participants per group.
We will stop after data from 100 researchers has been collected.
Two conditions. In one, researchers receive automated feedback. In the control condition, they do not receive feedback.
We will code all manuscripts for mistakes, and count the total number of mistakes per manuscript.
We will perform an independent t-test on the number of mistakes in each group.

We will conduct two-way ANOVAs with gender and condition as IVs and all the seven DVs.

(1) Negative binomial regression to examine the effect of emotion condition on number of items counted (count data). The awe condition will be compared to the joy and control conditions.
(2) Fisher's exact test (chi-square test) to examine the association between emotion condition and probability of donating one's raffle ticket. We will calculate odds ratios comparing the awe condition to the joy and control conditions.
We will interpret effects as significant if p < .05
No exclusions are expected.
No missing data is expected.

We also measured the expertise of researchers (in years) to explore whether the automated tool would be more useful, the less research experience researchers had. We also asked researchers to rate how useful they found the checklist or app on a scale from 1 (not at all) to 7 (extremely useful).

No, no data have been collected for this study yet.

It's complicated. We have already collected some data but explain in Question 8 why readers may consider this a valid pre-registration nevertheless.

Seven questions (all anchored at 1 = not at all and 7 = very much, with the exception of the introversion question which will be anchored at 1 = very introverted and 7 = very extroverted):
Do you think this person is overweight?
Do you think this person takes care of themselves?
Do you think this person is successful at work?
Do you think this person has an attractive face?
Do you think this person is clinically depressed? (manipulation check)
Do you think this person is introverted or extroverted?

Prosocial helping will be measured in two ways:
(1) Number of food items counted in an effortful task that benefits refugee families. The more items counted, the more participants help refugees. Item count can range from 0 (in case a participant did not count any items) to 210 (in case a participant counted all items).
(2) Probability of donating a raffle ticket that participants will receive as reward for their participation. Donating the ticket to a refugee family (vs. not) indicates prosocial helping.

Participants who respond "Yes" to the question "Have you ever been on the planet Jupiter?" will be excluded from analyses.

Participants who will not respond to our main dependent variables (food item count, ticket donation) will be excluded from the analyses.

* Variables collected for exploratory purposes: 5 items measuring the psychological experience of "small self"; 2 items measuring overlap between self & a friend as well as self & a stranger; 1 item measuring whether the participant had previously seen the video; 1 item measuring whether the participant could understand the language of the song lyrics in the awe condition
* Variables collected as manipulation/validity check: 6 items measuring experienced emotions in response to the film clip
* Why this should be taken as a valid pre-registration: Although data collection started before pre-registering this study, we have finalized neither the data collection nor the analyses.
